subject: Chemistry
title: Predict the Product: Haloalkane Preparation Questions Solved
summary: Three questions solve almost every "predict the product" problem: (1) what is the reagent? (2) which bond breaks? (3) where does the halogen go? In this lesson: identify the reagent, the bond that breaks, and where the halogen goes. Reagent toolkit, three traps (SOCl2, the peroxide effect, toluene light vs dark) and four questions solved on the board: SOCl2 on propan-1-ol, HBr on propene with and without peroxide, the Finkelstein reaction, and toluene + Cl2 in the dark vs sunlight.

notes.title: Predict the Product
notes.blurb: the reagent toolkit, three traps, solved questions

keyPoints: **The trick**: Read the **reagent** first. Then the **condition** (light, dark, peroxide).
**Alcohols**: SOCl₂: gases escape → **pure** product. PCl₅ / HX also replace **OH**.
**Alkenes + HBr**: Markovnikov: via the **2° carbocation**. Peroxide flips **HBr only**.
**Exchange**: Finkelstein: **dry acetone**, NaCl↓. Swarts: metallic fluoride, **heat**.

list: ✗ SOCl₂ gives a pure product because SO₂ and HCl escape as gases.
✗ Peroxide reverses the addition only for HBr (not HCl or HI).
✗ Toluene + Cl₂: light → side chain; dark + Lewis acid → ring.

blocks.p: **Q2.** CH₃CH=CH₂ + HBr → CH₃CHBrCH₃ (**2-bromopropane**): H adds to C1, Br to C2 through the more stable 2° carbocation. With peroxide: CH₃CH₂CH₂Br (**1-bromopropane**).
**Q4.** Toluene + Cl₂: (a) FeCl₃, dark → **o- and p-chlorotoluene**; (b) sunlight → **benzyl chloride**.

simulation.reason: The idea is a fixed sequence of steps drawn in the video and the notes; there is no continuous variable for a student to explore.

pyq.q: The product (C) in the reaction sequence CH₃–CH₂–CH₂–Br —KOH(alc), Δ→ A —HBr→ B —KOH(aq), Δ→ C is:
pyq.explain: Propan-2-ol A = propene (elimination); B = 2-bromopropane (Markovnikov); C = propan-2-ol (substitution by OH⁻).
